title: Dead Star Offers a Glimpse Into Our Solar System’s Future - Nautilus
author: Jake Currie
text:
Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyDead Star Offers a Glimpse Into Our Solar System’s FutureA ring of debris hints at planetary survivorsJCBy Jake Currie5:00 PM CDT on October 28, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThis illustration shows a debris disc around the white dwarf J1328−1450 –– the dead core of a star similar to our Sun that expelled its outer layers at the end of its lifetime. The star was suspected to have a planetary system that was vaporised to rubble as the star died, and this debris ended up arranged in a disc like the one shown here. The disc contains both gas and dust, but the gas appears to be arranged in a unique way. Using the X-shooter instrument on ESO’s Very Large Telescope (VLT) astronomers measured the speed of the gas orbiting the white dwarf, and found that it moves at two distinct speeds. This indicates that the gas is distributed in two concentric discs with a gap in between. The most likely explanation is that these two gaseous discs are maintained by two planetesimals that survived the death of the star. As they orbit the white dwarf they interact with dust grains in the disc, releasing gas in the process, shown here as luminous trails.
A team of astronomers using the European Southern Observatory’s Very Large Telescope recently spotted something curious. Observing a white dwarf (J1328−1450) located roughly 1,600 light-years from Earth, the team noticed it was surrounded by a rare disc of debris. According to their analysis, recently published in Nature Astronomy, it could offer a glimpse into the future of our solar system. When a star like our sun approaches the end of its life, it first expands into a red giant, then sheds its outer layers, collapsing into a superdense white dwarf. During the dramatic expansion, any closely orbiting planets may be engulfed and torn apart (R.I.P. Earth). The team says this disc of debris surrounding white dwarf J1328−1450 is likely made up of the remnants of those planets.Read more: “This Lion-Like Nebula Has Cosmic Dust for a Mane and a Dying Star for a Face”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
